purpose: Pre-deploy completion-triad drift check. assertCompletionTriad in api/lib/enum-domains.ts:141-185 rejects mutations where status/completed/completed_at disagree. This audit verifies existing D1 state before activating validators.

done_no_completed.query: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM tasks WHERE status='done' AND completed != 1

completed_not_done.query: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM tasks WHERE completed = 1 AND status != 'done'

completed_at_not_done.note: Subset of completed_not_done (57 of 61 deleted rows also have completed_at set)

deleted_rows.reason: assertCompletionTriad explicitly skips when resulting status='deleted' (api/lib/enum-domains.ts:155: 'Tombstones are not completions'). These rows will never trip the validator regardless of future mutations.

done_no_completed.reason: The validator only fires when an incoming mutation TOUCHES a completion field (status, completed, or completed_at). A mutation that updates an unrelated field (e.g. due_date) on this row is NOT blocked. Only a mutation that also touches one of the three completion fields triggers the check — and such a mutation would need to resolve the triad anyway.

rationale: 61 of 62 violations are status='deleted' rows that the validator explicitly exempts. The 1 genuine violation (task_01KQGKXAWAPCQET3MCXFYAKMA9: done but completed=0) will only block a future mutation that specifically touches a completion field on that row. No existing automation touches that row's completion fields — it is a legacy inconsistency from pre-A3. If Nick wants to clean it up proactively, the fix is: update tasks SET completed=1, completed_at='<timestamp>' WHERE id='task_01KQGKXAWAPCQET3MCXFYAKMA9'.
